description: The wiring test's 'healthy slot' fixture proves REQ-AS-002's second acceptance criterion ('A trace ending in ANY action != "skip" line ... -> NOT barren, regardless of how many skip lines precede it') for the wrong reason. mk_healthy_trace() writes 15 skip lines + 1 trailing live-pass line = 16 TOTAL lines, against minRun=20 in the registry fixture. Since len(trace_tail) < min_run is the FIRST short-circuit in is_fresh_but_barren (earning-health.py:42-43), slot-b's 'OK' result in test_earning_health_allslots.sh is produced purely by insufficient trace length -- the exact same 'OK' would be logged even with ZERO skip lines, or even if the trailing-live-pass-overrides-prior-skips logic in the wiring script were completely broken. The WIRING layer (the actual shell script + tail + python3 subprocess pipe under test here) never exercises a full min_run-length trace that ends in a non-skip line through the real end-to-end path. (The underlying PURE predicate is correctly proven at the exact 20-line boundary at the unit level in skills/self/tests/test_earning_health.py:61-63 -- 19 skips + 1 live_pass = exactly min_run=20 -- so this is a wiring-test-only weakness, not a demonstrated production defect, but it means REQ-AS-002's acceptance criterion #2 is NOT actually proven through the artifact this sprint added (earning-health-allslots.sh), only assumed to carry over correctly.)

evidence.snippet:
mk_healthy_trace(){
  local out="$1"
  : > "$out"
  for i in $(seq 1 15); do
    printf '{"ts":"2026-07-08T%02d:00:00Z","action":"skip","reason":"%s"}\n' "$((i % 24))" "$REASON_A" >> "$out"
  done
  printf '{"ts":"2026-07-10T14:04:39Z","action":"live-pass","exit":0,"note":"WAIT"}\n' >> "$out"
}
